concepts.name: Economics as a Social Science
concepts.description: Economics is a social science that studies how individuals and societies utilize limited resources to satisfy unlimited wants. It examines production, consumption, exchange, and distribution of goods and services.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define economics and explain why it is considered a social science.

concepts.name: Scarcity and Choice
concepts.description: Resources are limited while human wants are unlimited, making scarcity a fundamental economic problem. Individuals and societies must make choices about resource allocation.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the relationship between scarcity and economic choice.

concepts.name: Scope of Economics
concepts.description: Economics studies the behavior of consumers, producers, governments, and markets at both individual and national levels.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to describe the scope of economics using practical examples.

concepts.name: Problem of Resource Allocation
concepts.description: Every economy faces the challenge of allocating scarce resources efficiently to maximize satisfaction and economic welfare.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain why efficient allocation of resources is necessary.

concepts.name: Central Economic Problems
concepts.description: Every economy must answer three fundamental questions: what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and explain the three central economic problems.

concepts.name: Opportunity Cost
concepts.description: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is sacrificed when making an economic choice.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate and interpret opportunity cost in simple economic situations.

concepts.name: Microeconomics
concepts.description: Microeconomics studies the economic behavior of individual consumers, firms, and specific markets.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish microeconomic issues from macroeconomic issues.

concepts.name: Macroeconomics
concepts.description: Macroeconomics focuses on the economy as a whole, including national income, inflation, unemployment, and economic growth.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the scope of macroeconomics.

concepts.name: Economics in Daily Life
concepts.description: Economic principles influence personal decisions regarding income, spending, saving, investment, and consumption.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate economic concepts to everyday decision-making.

concepts.name: Role in National Development
concepts.description: Economics helps governments formulate policies for employment, growth, poverty reduction, and efficient resource utilization.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the importance of economics in national development.

concepts.name: Decision Making
concepts.description: Economic reasoning enables individuals, businesses, and governments to make informed choices by evaluating costs and benefits.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply economic reasoning to simple decision-making situations.

concepts.name: Introduction to Economics
concepts.description: This chapter introduces the meaning, nature, scope, branches, and importance of economics while emphasizing scarcity, choice, and efficient resource allocation.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the fundamental concepts of economics and apply them to basic real-world situations.
